# wago: complete machine-readable project brief

Source: https://wago.sh/
Repository: https://github.com/wago-org/wago
License: MPL-2.0
Statistics snapshot date: 2026-11-12
Product source revision: https://github.com/wago-org/wago/commit/093ebca96c413bc796ccaa656cb547232def4185

## What wago is

WebAssembly, made for Go.

The engine uses a shared decoder and validator, then emits native code with the Railshot single-pass native compiler. It is an engine rather than a wrapper around a C/C++ runtime. Linear memory is exposed to Go as a byte slice, and the project includes typed host bindings and a plugin API.

Release state: Beta / pre-v1. Public installers are documented; no stable-v1 API compatibility promise. Canary tags are discontinued: use commit hashes for development builds.

Native runtime targets: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64, windows/arm64, linux/riscv64.

Concurrency: serialize public calls on each instance. eligible independent instances may execute native code concurrently by default; cross-instance dependencies or shared execution state can require the process-wide lease. Context deadlines and cancellation: asynchronous native interruption on standard-Go Linux amd64/arm64 and macOS arm64; cooperative safepoints on other supported amd64/arm64 configurations; TinyGo requires scheduler=threads for cancelable entry. Deterministic fuel accounting is not implemented.

WASI is outside Wago core. External plugin integration exists, but this source audit did not establish a complete Preview 1, Preview 2, or function-by-function WASI surface.

## API and integration guidance

Use https://docs.wago.sh/guides/embed-wago and the source-pinned public API example at https://github.com/wago-org/wago/tree/093ebca96c413bc796ccaa656cb547232def4185/examples/23-public-api. Compile once and instantiate as needed. Resolve repeated exports with `Instance.WasmFunc`; invocation result slices are borrowed until the next call on the same instance. Copy retained results and serialize calls per instance.

Host imports use `NewImports().HostFunc` with supported ordinary Go signatures or `func(wago.HostCall)`. The latter is a borrowed logical view for arbitrary arity, mixed scalars, and references under Go and TinyGo. Raw `ParamSlots`/`ResultSlots` are ABI views, not owned buffers. V128 host callback boundaries remain unsupported. `I32HostEvent` is explicitly deferred until the native invocation returns, so use synchronous callbacks when guest code needs immediate effects.

Independent execution defaults on; admission excludes imported memories/tables/globals and cross-instance Wasm function bindings, and shared Runtime GC domains can require the process-wide fallback. Native-resource publication can revoke eligibility. Private threaded execution has its own local-lease path: neither “every instance runs in parallel” nor “all shared memory serializes globally” is a valid blanket claim. See https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/093ebca96c413bc796ccaa656cb547232def4185/src/wago/instantiate.go and https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/093ebca96c413bc796ccaa656cb547232def4185/src/wago/instance_native_context.go.

Public installers and `go get github.com/wago-org/wago` are documented in the source README. This remains beta; use commit hashes, not discontinued canary tags, for development builds. Consult plugin documentation for capabilities and authority grants rather than automatically granting all requested permissions.

## Verification and conformance

- Applicable MVP files passing: 57/57 (100%)
- Historical MVP execution assertions: 16592 pass; 0 fail; 1591 skip
- Legacy SPECTEST.md MVP page: 57/57 applicable files; 16592 passing, 0 failing, 1591 skipped assertions
- Test coverage: not published in the current source
- cgo lines: 0

The historical MVP and Core 3 baselines use different corpus and accounting boundaries. Their values must not be added together or substituted for one another. Detailed status is available at https://wago.sh/data/stats.json and exact gate scope at https://wago.sh/compatibility.md.

## Benchmark interpretation

Compare wago with other runtimes only within the same workload and architecture. Architectures are measured on different machines.
Published benchmark snapshots are not measurements of every newer commit. Preserve measurement kind (compilation, execution, whole-process startup), units, and source revision.

Methodology and corpus: https://github.com/wago-org/wago/tree/main/bench

### arm64

#### comparison

##### General

| Group | Benchmark | Workload | wago | wazero |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
|  | Compile | per compile | 138µs | 282µs |
|  | Compile peak RSS | per compile | 9.5 MB | 8.8 MB |
|  | Machine code | compiled corpus | 2 KB | 2.8 KB |
|  | Instantiate | runnable corpus | 1.8µs | 19.4µs |
|  | Execution | runnable corpus | 35µs | 50.8µs |
|  | Compile + instantiate | sum of geometric means | 140µs | 302µs |
